text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers.
- Insurers Bundeslaender and Austria-Collegialitaet are to merge under a holding to become Austria's number one insurer.
- Gabriele Hecht, a tax counsellor, is to succeed Wolfgang Bachmayer as the Liberal Forum's number one candidate in the October 13 Vienna elections.
- Wages are to rise 1.6 percent in Austria' paper industry.
- Austria should have greater autonomy to hand out subsidies within the European Union and pay less into EU coffers, the Chamber of Economy says.
- EBRD and Bank Austria are to work together in Croatia.
- Bank Austria head Gerhard Randa said the bank would put forward an offer for Hungary's Magyar Hitel Bank by mid-October.
- Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky has not yet been in contact with hospitalised President Thomas Klestil. Doctors say the president should stay in hospital at least until the end of the week.
- Both Chancellor Franz Vranitzky and Interior Minister Caspar Einem have been named as targets of a guerilla threat to blow up prominent people in Austria and abroad.
- Former Finance Minister Hannes Androsch is holding talks with U.S. tyre maker Goodyear about taking over German Continental's Austrian unit Semperit.
- Bank Austria will earn more than a billion schillings abroad in 1996, the bank's head Gerhard Randa said.
- The number of Austrian insolvencies has risen 22 percent in the first nine months of 1996 compared to the same period last year.
- Few stock exchanges will survive the introduction of single currency Euro. However, investors should benefit from monetary union.
- Provincial energy supplier EVN is to cut jobs by 20 percent by the year 2000 in preparation for the liberalised market.
